title: Turn your coding agent's steps into reusable commands
summary: A developer turned his Claude coding routine into eight reusable commands that interview him, write specs and tickets, build test-first, review and open pull requests.
agent_role: The agent interviews the developer, writes specs and tickets, builds each ticket test-first, reviews and opens pull requests; the developer answers questions and approves risky changes.
what_they_did: The developer packed his coding routine into reusable commands. One interviews him about a feature until no questions remain. Others turn that into a spec and small tickets, build each ticket with tests first, and review the changes. Hard checks block commits if tests fail or secrets show up.
how_it_went: The author says the debug rule, reproducing a bug before guessing causes, stopped the agent fixing the first likely cause. He reports no other numbers.
worth_knowing: His key idea: turn every 'please remember to' into a check that fails. Written reminders get skipped under pressure; failing checks do not.
prompt: Before building [feature], interview me in rounds until the plan has no open questions, suggesting an answer for each. Then write a short spec in [specs folder] and split it into small tickets with clear order. Build the first unblocked ticket test-first, run the project's lint, type checks and tests, and stop if any fail. Show me the diff and wait for my approval before committing, pushing or opening a pull request.

curation.rationale: A real, shared coding-agent workflow with code, but it is one more spec-and-tickets flow with no measured results.
